chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Hamzah who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who had a debt upon another man. A man came to him and bought from him for a price (or 'for a sum'), then he went to the one who owed the debt and said to him, 'Give me what so-and-so has upon you, for I have bought it from him.' How should the repayment be in that case? He (Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him) said to him, 'The man who owes the debt should return to him the wealth that he bought from the man who has the debt upon him.'

key_terms.بِعَرْضٍ: for a price / for a sum

ai.seo_question: How is a debt settled when the creditor sells the debt to a third party?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the mechanism of debt assignment (hiwalah) by instructing the debtor to repay the buyer directly, thereby validating the transfer of the creditor's right. This ruling underscores the legal validity of selling financial claims in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the debtor's obligation is discharged upon payment to the new holder. The narration highlights the practical application of contract law in early Islamic society, emphasizing clarity in ownership transfer to prevent disputes.
